plan.note: The 90 day plan, data first. The connectors are just tools; the plan is organized around what gets captured and what gets done with it. Order: capture your own data, capture competitor data, act on what the data says, then re capture to prove movement. Every task has an owner (you, client, ai), a checkable done criterion, and blocked items carry their workaround. The console reads and writes this file.

phases.name: Capture your data
phases.goal: Every first party source lands in data/ with a baseline number. Nothing gets decided until this exists.

tasks.title: Search Console: verify, share access, pull 90 days of queries and positions
tasks.done: gsc-queries.json populated; we know every search Wolff already appears for

tasks.title: Google Analytics: access and pull traffic, conversions, enquiry paths
tasks.done: We know which pages produce enquiries today, even if the answer is none

tasks.title: Website data: fresh crawl, site check baseline, speed scores per template
tasks.done: Baseline recorded: failure count, word counts, speed scores, saved as day 1 numbers

tasks.title: Business model data: permits from CSLB, Rocklin and Placer County records, BuildZoom history, verified company facts
tasks.done: data/projects.json holds the permit record; zero UNVERIFIED flags left in company.json after the client facts call

tasks.title: Structured data online: what exists about Wolff across the web, schema on site, every profile and citation
tasks.done: Citation audit complete; every profile graded live, weak, or unclaimed, and the SF Wolff confusion points mapped

tasks.title: Duda API keys from Bullsai, requested in the same conversation as the data access
tasks.done: Keys in .env and a test diff runs. Workaround if refused: publishing goes manual from the Preview screen, nothing waits

phases.name: Capture competitor data
phases.goal: Every target search has a named owner, a measured volume, and a season. The win scores stop being judgment.

tasks.title: SERP capture: who ranks for all 17 target searches, with which pages and what proof
tasks.done: competitors.json updated from live results, not from the audit snapshot

tasks.title: Competitor inventory: review counts, published cost ranges, page structures, new entrants
tasks.done: Each competitor row lists what they own and the counter, verified this month

tasks.title: Search volumes and difficulty for every target query
tasks.done: Win scores rescored as measured; the plan order reflects real demand

tasks.title: Seasonality: five years of California interest per service
tasks.done: Each service has peak months and a publish by date the content calendar obeys

tasks.title: AI citation baseline: ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Copilot the six target questions, log who gets named today
tasks.done: Day 1 citation log saved so day 90 has something honest to compare against

phases.name: Act on what the data says
phases.goal: Fixes and pages ship in the order the captured data dictates. Success: failures near zero and Wolff appears for kitchen remodel Granite Bay, up from nowhere.

tasks.title: Publish the 17 page fix payload including the blog bug
tasks.done: Re crawl shows failures under 10; blog no longer wears the careers title

tasks.title: The three missing service pages, built with captured proof: kitchen first, then full home, then additions and ADU
tasks.done: Each indexed, passing site check, carrying real investment bands and sourced reviews

tasks.title: Projects hub; case studies moved to service and city slugs with redirects
tasks.done: Old addresses 301 to new ones; nav no longer points at nothing

tasks.title: Testimonials rebuilt with verified review schema
tasks.done: Star eligibility confirmed; every review traceable to a live source

tasks.title: Houzz Rocklin claimed, GBP rebuilt, every weak citation fixed
tasks.done: Citation audit reports zero weak and zero unclaimed; GBP Q&A seeded with the cost questions

phases.name: Prove it, then reload
phases.goal: Publish the proof content the season calls for, re capture everything, and aim the next 90 days with numbers.

tasks.title: Cost guide with real investment bands, timed to the captured seasonality
tasks.done: Live before the next research peak; GVD is no longer the only local number an AI can cite

tasks.title: Permit and timeline answers on the process page, built from the permit record

competitors.note: The competitive set from the audit: who actually appeared for 'luxury kitchen remodel Granite Bay CA contractor' and adjacent money terms, plus the brand-name competitor. Every claim here traces to research/Construction website.docx. Refresh quarterly or when a new name enters the local pack.

owns: cost answers: publishes $35,000 to $150,000+ ranges an LLM can cite
competitors.wolffAngle: Cannot be out reviewed. Beat with specificity: named PM, permit record, real investment bands with scope attached, deeper single reviews.

competitors.name: Capital Construction
competitors.wolffAngle: Same playbook as GVD; same counter.

competitors.wolffAngle: Showroom volume brand; does not compete for $150k+ structural remodels. Qualification content separates the markets.

competitors.wolffAngle: Closest model to Wolff. Wolff's verifiable evidence layer (license, permits, memberships, named team) is the differentiator.

owns: dedicated service or city pages that surfaced in the target SERP

competitors.name: AAR Construction
owns: dedicated service or city pages that surfaced in the target SERP

competitors.name: Tankersley Construction
owns: dedicated service or city pages that surfaced in the target SERP
competitors.wolffAngle: Loses on luxury proof depth and review specificity.

competitors.name: Wolff Construction (San Francisco)

competitors.keyFinding: On the audited money query, seven competitors appeared and Wolff appeared nowhere. Every competitor that ranks has dedicated service or service by city pages. Wolff has zero. That is the structural gap the opportunity matrix closes.

opportunities.note: The opportunity matrix: customer intent x service x market, scored against who owns the answer today and what Wolff can credibly claim. score = demand (1-5) x fit to Wolff's model (1-5) x winnability vs incumbent (1-5), max 125. This file drives prioritization; the console sorts by it. Sources: research/profile-and-plan.md intents 1-6, the audit's competitor findings, data/questions.json clusters.

structure.note: The target information architecture. Status per node: live-ok (exists, healthy), live-weak (exists, needs work), staged (fix in page-updates.json), missing (must be built). The rule that produced it: every customer intent gets a permanent page, blog posts support service pages (spokes to hubs), projects prove services, people prove the entity, and every page is at most 2 clicks from home.
linkingRules: Service pages link to: their proof projects, their supporting blog posts, relevant reviews, the process page, and the qualifying CTA
Blog posts link UP to their service page (hub), never only sideways
Project pages link to: their service page, their city page (when live), the team members who ran the job, and the client review
Team pages link to: projects they ran and the about page; the about page is the entity home
No orphans: every indexable page reachable from nav or a hub in 2 clicks

tree.role: Market + service hub. Must name the full service area.

children.role: City page: after service pages exist
Entity home: history, license, address, memberships
Review hub with sourced schema; reviews syndicate to service pages

workers.note: The AI worker fleet. Each worker is a scoped agent job: a mission, the sources it audits, the files it writes, and a cadence. scripts/run-worker.js generates the work order (mission + guardrails + current data + output contract) that a Claude or Codex agent executes. Workers write to data/ and reports/ only; nothing ships without the validator and human approval. Mode: auto = runs locally with no agent, agent = needs an AI worker, hybrid = agent plus local scripts.

workers.name: GBP Auditor
workers.audits: Google Business Profile: categories, services, hours, photos and geotags, Q&A, review velocity and owner responses, NAP match against data/company.json
sources: Google Maps local pack for target queries
workers.brief: Audit the Wolff Construction GBP as a customer and as an engine. Score: correct categories for luxury remodeling; services list matching data/services.json; photos of real projects with geotags; Q&A seeded with the cost and timeline questions from data/questions.json; every review answered in the owner voice; exact NAP match with the site and every citation. Flag anything that conflicts with the Rocklin entity or leaks toward the San Francisco Wolff. Output: findings ranked by impact, each with the exact fix.

workers.name: Competitor Monitor
workers.audits: The live SERP set for every opportunity query: who ranks, what pages they launched, review counts, new entrants
workers.brief: Re-run every target query in data/opportunities.json. For each: record who appears, which URL, and what proof they show. Diff against data/competitors.json: new entrants, new pages, review count changes, cost content changes. Update the file and write the delta report. Flag any query where Wolff now appears, with position.

workers.name: Market Insight Worker
workers.audits: Demand and conversation: what Placer County homeowners ask and where, seasonality, price expectations
workers.brief: Find the questions real homeowners in the service area are asking that data/questions.json does not cover. Evidence per question: where it was asked, how often the theme recurs, what answer exists today. Propose demand score adjustments to data/opportunities.json with the evidence attached. Never invent volume numbers; cite the thread or the trend line.

workers.name: Project and Permit Historian
workers.audits: Government and public records: CSLB license standing, Rocklin and Placer County permit records, BuildZoom history. Old projects become the proof layer.
sources: City of Rocklin and Placer County permit portals
workers.brief: Build the verifiable project record. Confirm CSLB 1056036 standing and bond status. Pull every permit attributable to Wolff: date, jurisdiction, scope class, valuation band where public. Cross reference BuildZoom. Produce data/projects.json rows: city, year, scope, permit reference. Street addresses NEVER ship; neighborhood and city only. This file feeds case study pages, the top 1 percent claim, and every stat the site publishes.

workers.name: SEO Data Connector
workers.audits: Connected performance data: Search Console queries and pages, GA4 conversions, rank positions for the opportunity set
sources: Google Search Console API or export
manual rank checks until API access lands
workers.brief: Ingest the latest GSC and GA4 exports into data/performance/. Recompute: which opportunity queries have impressions, which pages earn clicks, which consultations trace to which page. Replace judgment demand scores in data/opportunities.json with measured ones, marking each score measured or estimated. The monthly report reads from these files.

workers.name: Planner
workers.audits: Everything the other workers wrote, against the plan
workers.brief: Read every worker output since the last planning pass. Reprioritize data/plan.json: what moved, what is blocked, what the opportunity scores now say to build next. Stage the next unit of work in data/page-updates.json or a content branch. One unit per PR. Every staged claim must trace to a data file per CLAUDE.md rule 1.

workers.name: Adversarial Reviewer
workers.audits: Every PR before merge, against CLAUDE.md and the data files
workers.brief: Attack the PR. Find: claims without a data source, review text not verbatim from data/reviews.json, UNVERIFIED fields shipping, banned language, dash characters in copy, titles without geo tokens, schema not generated from data. Approve only when nothing survives. Alternate implementer and reviewer roles between agents on every PR.

workers.name: Deployer
workers.audits: The gap between approved staged changes and the live site
writes: the Duda draft, then production on publish
workers.brief: Run the validator; refuse on failure. Dry run the diff, apply on recorded human approval, republish, submit the updated URLs to IndexNow so Bing and the AI engines recrawl immediately, then schedule the verify crawl. Log every push with the commit hash it came from.
